children: Palm oil prices closed lower, weighed by weaker soybean oil and crude oil prices, alongside softer Dalian vegetable oils and concerns over slowing Malaysian export demand, says David Ng, a trader at Kuala Lumpur-based Iceberg X. Ng expects crude palm oil futures to find support at around 4,400 ringgit a ton and face resistance at 4,600 ringgit a ton. The market sentiment will likely remain cautious amid weaker competing vegetable oils and energy prices, he adds. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for February delivery ended 113 ringgit lower at 4,434 ringgit a ton. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
